submitted.rationale: Index 136 (Cr0.10 Fe0.63 V0.27) had the highest measured EQE, 0.149%. MACE puts FeVO4 on the hull, and MEGNet gives it an HSE gap of ~2.75 eV, just above the 2.72 eV photons. Fe-rich compositions probably add Fe2O3 (gap ~2.1 eV), which absorbs 455 nm light better. This fits the Fe-rich film beating the Fe:V ~1:1 and Cr-rich films.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 0.097%. At Fe:V ~1:1 (FeVO4-like) the band gap sits at the photon energy, so absorption is marginal.
Measured EQE 0.088%. Adding Cr did not help.

consultations.verdict: Weak support: MEGNet HSE gap 2.75 eV for mp-504509 is right at the 2.72 eV photon energy, so absorption would be marginal. That points to a vanadate with the smallest possible gap. Fe:V ~1:1 with low Cr (FeVO4-like) is the prior-favored region.

Uninformative-to-weak: the PBE gap is 2.08 eV and HSE is 2.75 eV, so absorption at 2.72 eV is marginal. Cr addition may improve visible absorption. I'm testing the Cr-rich middle as contrast to index 90.

Support: MACE puts FeVO4 on the hull (Ehull 0). Its gap (~2.75 eV HSE) sits at the edge of 2.72 eV photons, which limits absorption. Fe-rich compositions should give FeVO4 plus Fe2O3 (gap ~2.1 eV), with stronger 455 nm absorption and a possible heterojunction. That makes it a good final probe for beating index 90.
